stem: (Select TWO.) Dunbeath Systems asks a new hire to explain, in their own words, TWO different jobs the state file does besides simply existing.

choices.text: It records which already-created real object corresponds to a specific resource block, so re-running a command does not create a duplicate.
It keeps track of metadata, such as resource dependencies, so Terraform still knows the correct order for a change even if the configuration was later edited.
It stores a full daily backup of every resource's own data, such as a database's rows, in case a resource needs to be restored.
It enforces which team members are allowed to run `terraform apply` against a given configuration.
It automatically rewrites the `.tf` configuration files so they always match whatever was actually built.

rationale: State's mapping purpose links an already-created real object to its resource block so a re-run does not duplicate it, and its metadata purpose keeps information such as dependencies available even after the configuration itself has changed. State tracks Terraform's own bookkeeping about resources, not an application's internal data such as database rows, so it is not a data backup mechanism. Access control over who may run `terraform apply` is not a function the state file performs. State also does not rewrite the `.tf` configuration files; configuration stays the desired-state input while state is a separate record of what was actually built.
